target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM (Engineering, Physics, Mathematics)

sections.title: The Bridge from Scalars to Matrices
lecture_lines: Recall the Taylor series for the scalar exponential $e^x$.
This formula uses basic addition and multiplication operations.
We can replace the scalar $x$ with matrix $A$.
Notice the scalar 1 becomes the identity matrix $I$.
The matrix exponential describes a proportional growth process.
animations: Show the scalar Taylor series: $e^x = 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2!} + \dots$ in White #FFFFFF.
Highlight the addition and multiplication symbols in the formula in Cyan #00FFFF.
Display matrix $A$ and its basic operations (addition/multiplication) in Green #00FF00.
Morph $x$ into $A$ in the series: $e^A = 1 + A + \frac{A^2}{2!} + \dots$.
Transition the scalar '1' into the identity matrix $I$ in Yellow #FFFF00.

sections.title: Visualizing the Sum: A Recursive Transformation
lecture_lines: Begin with a standard two-dimensional coordinate grid.
Matrix $A$ applies a linear transformation to the grid.
$e^A$ represents the accumulated sum of these transformations.
animations: Display a 2x2 matrix with 'e' raised to each element, then cross it out with a Red #FF0000 'X'.
Show the expansion $I + A + \frac{A^2}{2!} + \frac{A^3}{3!} + \dots$ in White #FFFFFF.
Animate a unit square transforming via $A$ (Green #00FF00) then $A^2$ (Blue #0000FF).
Visualize the terms $I$, $A$, and $A^2/2$ as vectors being added head-to-tail in Orange #FFA500.
Show the resulting sum $e^A$ as a smooth, final transformation of the original grid in Cyan #00FFFF.

sections.title: The Shortcut: Diagonalization
lecture_lines: Calculating an infinite sum of matrices is very difficult.
If matrix $A$ is diagonalizable, use $A = PDP^{-1}$.
The formula for $e^A$ simplifies using this decomposition.
We only need to exponentiate the diagonal elements.
Reassembling these matrices gives the final result quickly.
animations: Display matrix $A$ alongside a complex summation $\sum A^n/n!$ with a Red #FF0000 'Difficult' tag.
Show the decomposition $A = PDP^{-1}$ with $D$ highlighted in Yellow #FFFF00.
Display the equation $e^A = P e^D P^{-1}$ in White #FFFFFF.
Animate the diagonal elements $d_i$ of $D$ transforming into $e^{d_i}$ in Green #00FF00.
Assemble $P, e^D, P^{-1}$ into the final matrix $e^A$ in Orange #FFA500.

sections.title: Application: The Autonomous Drone Path
lecture_lines: The equation $dx/dt$ equals $Ax$ defines the system's change.
The solution uses the matrix exponential $e^{At}$.
Aero-Bot begins at its initial position $x(0)$.
The drone follows a path determined by the exponential.
This visualizes the continuous evolution of the system's state.
animations: Show the equation $dx/dt = Ax$ morphing into its solution $x(t) = e^{At}x(0)$ in Yellow #FFFF00.
Place a drone icon at the origin of a coordinate system in White #FFFFFF.
Animate the drone moving along a curved path representing $e^{At}$ in Cyan #00FFFF.

sections.title: Summary and Key Takeaways
lecture_lines: First, $e^A$ is defined by a matrix power series.
Second, diagonalization provides a fast way to compute it.
Finally, it solves continuous state evolution in physical systems.
